name: Com ga
summary: Chicken and yellow rice. In Hoi An the chicken is shredded and the rice takes turmeric and broth. Da Nang also serves a fried plate.
origin: Hoi An. Vietnam Tourism says the plate is believed to come from Hainanese chicken rice.
history: Vietnam Tourism says Hoi An’s cơm gà is believed to come from a Hainanese dish brought by Chinese immigrants, the same family of chicken rice eaten in Singapore, Thailand, and Malaysia.
culture: Hoi An’s food page treats the plate as a dish of the old trading port: a Chinese technique, then Vietnamese sides. You order it when you want rice instead of the town’s noodles.
texture: In Hoi An the chicken is poached and shredded. The rice is a yellow pilaf cooked with chicken broth and turmeric. Herbs, a bowl of chicken soup, and a sour papaya salad come with the plate.
taste: The salad is sour. The rice is fragrant from the broth and the turmeric.
howToEat: Eat the shredded chicken with the rice, the herbs, and the papaya salad. Leave the soup in its bowl.
The photograph is a fried chicken-rice plate. It is not the shredded Hoi An plate.
In Da Nang, ask which chicken the shop is cooking. Hồng Ngọc, 193 Nguyễn Chí Thanh, is the Hong Kong-style plate. Tú Tài, 62 Hải Phòng, is the Hoi An-style plate.

The 16 Apr 2024 Da Nang page says chicken rice is an old Da Nang plate and is best known in Tam Kỳ and Hội An: fragrant rice, soft chicken, chicken offal, shredded green papaya, rau răm, and a little simmered chili sauce.
where: Eat the shredded plate in Hoi An.
Hồng Ngọc, 193 Nguyễn Chí Thanh, is the Hong Kong-style plate. Tú Tài, 62 Hải Phòng, is the Hoi An-style plate.
seoTitle: Com ga — chicken rice in Hoi An and Da Nang
seoDescription: Hoi An’s com ga is shredded poached chicken, turmeric rice, herbs, soup, and sour papaya. In Da Nang, Hong Ngoc and Tu Tai cook two different plates.
